contradictions.preferred_canonical_value: These market-sizing figures are all Low confidence and should not be used in the same document as if they represent non-overlapping market layers. Standardise the market-size section to use only AAUI/AAJI primary data (High confidence) for insurance layer sizing, and explicitly mark all market research firm figures (NextMSC, Mordor, Ken Research) as directional-only with methodology-unknown caveats. Stage 5's Mordor USD 690M figure should carry the same Low-confidence and methodology-opaque flag as Stage 2's NextMSC figures.

contradictions.metric_or_actor: WHO/IDF presenteeism / productivity multipliers applied to Indonesia

values_compared.stage_1_pain_points_pp1_3: Singapore total economic cost per working-age diabetic USD 5,646 (2010) applied as comparator for Indonesia productivity cost argument
values_compared.stage_6_value_chain: ADA 2022 US presenteeism-to-absenteeism ratio (6.6:1) applied to derive Indonesia indirect cost upper bound

contradictions.description: Stage 1 uses Singapore productivity data as a proxy for Indonesia without a geography-mismatch flag — it is applied implicitly as a comparator ('USD 5,646 in 2010 per working-age diabetic') without noting that Singapore's per-capita GDP and wage structure is 5-7x Indonesia's, rendering the absolute dollar figure non-transferable. Stage 6 uses ADA 2022 US methodology more carefully, explicitly flagging it as an upper-bound reference requiring local wage calibration. The inconsistency is not in the data values themselves but in the transparency of the geography assumption: Stage 1 presents the Singapore figure as a comparator without a geography-mismatch warning; Stage 6 explicitly hedges the equivalent US methodology. A reader of Stage 1 could incorrectly apply the Singapore figure as Indonesia-relevant.
contradictions.preferred_canonical_value: Add a geography-mismatch caveat to Stage 1 PP 1.3's Singapore productivity figure: note explicitly that Singapore GDP per capita is ~5x Indonesia's and that the absolute USD figure is not transferable; use only the methodology (presenteeism-to-absenteeism ratio) as transferable, applying Indonesia wage data for the final calculation, consistent with Stage 6's treatment.

narrative: Six high-severity contradictions were found: the 13.6% medical cost inflation figure is used incorrectly in Stages 3 and 4 after DR5 corrected it to 14.6% in Stage 1 (Class C, immediate fix required); the Rp 100–400M private hospital AMI episode cost is cited as fact across Stages 1–5 without the primary-source gap and ASSUMED qualifier that DR4 established and Stage 6 correctly adopted (Class C, immediate); the IDF 73.2% undiagnosed rate conflicts with an ~81% implied rate from SKI 2023 data within Stage 6 without reconciliation (Class A, immediate); and three other load-bearing numeric claims carry unreconciled values across stages. None of these contradictions invalidate the hypothesis, but the three 'immediate' items must be resolved before the corpus is cited in a commercial or investor context.
